# R objects {#robjectschap}
![](/images/RObjects.png){style="width:200px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: white 5px solid" fig-align="center"}

In the [foundations part](/foundations/intro.qmd) you learnt how to create a <u id='variable_tooltip'>__variable__</u>. 
This consisted of assigning (`<-`) an __object__ a name. 
In this chapter we will learn about __R objects__. 
There are two major R terminologies to learn to fully understand __R objects__, <u id='class_tooltip'>__Class__</u> and <u id='data_structure_tooltip'>__Data structure__</u>.

## Class
![](/images/category.png){style="width:200px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: white 5px solid" fig-align="center"}

A R <u id='class_tooltip'>__Class__</u> refers to the type of data.
There are six basic <u id='class_tooltip'>__classes__</u> in R (Also known as the __atomic <u id='class_tooltip'>classes</u>__). 
These materials cover:

- [**Numerics**](/objects/numeric.qmd): Numbers
  - Numeric can come in the form of <u id='integer_tooltip'>__integers__</u> and <u id='double_tooltip'>__doubles__</u>
- [**Strings**](/objects/string.qmd): Text
- [**Logicals**](/objects/logical.qmd): `TRUE` or `FALSE` 

There are also the <u id='class_tooltip'>classes</u> __complex__ and __raw__.

## Data structure
![](/images/data_structure){style="width:150px; background: white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"}

<u id='data_structure_tooltip'>__Data structures__</u> describe how data is structured in an __object__. 
We will focus on 3 main types of <u id='data_structure_tooltip'>__data structures__</u>.

- [**Scalar**](/objects/scalar.qmd): One value
- [**Vectors** & **Lists**](/objects/vectors_lists.qmd): 1-dimensional structures containing multiple values
- [**Data frames** & **Matrices**](/objects/data_frames_matrices.qmd): 2-dimensional structures containing multiple values over rows and columns (i.e. tabular)

## Code sections
In this part, and for the rest of the course, you will use code sections in your R scripts to separate pages, sections, and parts in this book.

First set your working directory to your course directory, create a script, and save it as __"2-Objects.R"__.

Next create a code section at the top of this script called __"Classes"__.

In other words have the below at the top of your script:

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Classes ####
```

